atomic_ism.description: Cold and warm atomic interstellar gas in the Milky Way and nearby star-forming environments, including H I 21 cm emission and absorption, HISA, HINSA, CNM and WNM, and the atomic-to-molecular transition.

molecular_clouds.description: Molecular clouds and molecular gas: cloud formation, structure, evolution, kinematics, CO and other molecular-line observations, dense gas, filaments, clumps, and cores.

star_formation.description: Star formation from cloud to core and young stellar object, including gravitational collapse, protostars, protostellar envelopes, accretion, clusters, and the interaction between young stars and their natal clouds.

feedback_bubbles.description: Stellar feedback acting on the interstellar medium, including Galactic H II regions, bubbles, cavities, shells, stellar winds, supernova feedback, triggered star formation, and interactions of expanding structures with molecular clouds.

turbulence.description: Turbulence and gas dynamics in the interstellar medium and molecular clouds, including velocity statistics, power spectra, structure functions, linewidths, density and column-density PDFs, and turbulent driving.

magnetic_fields.description: Magnetic fields in the interstellar medium and star-forming clouds, including dust polarization, Zeeman measurements, MHD, magnetic support, field morphology, and magnetic regulation of cloud and core evolution.

astrochemistry.description: Astrochemistry and molecular tracers in interstellar and star-forming gas, including chemical evolution, abundances, deuteration, ionization, cosmic-ray chemistry, and diagnostic molecular species in clouds and cores.

massive_star_formation.description: Massive star and cluster formation in dense molecular environments, including infrared dark clouds, massive clumps, high-mass protostars, hot cores, massive young stellar objects, and clustered star formation.

galactic_ism_surveys.description: Galactic interstellar medium on large scales, including Milky Way gas and dust surveys, Galactic structure traced by gas, H I and molecular-line surveys, three-dimensional dust and gas mapping, and datasets useful for ISM science.

ism_methods_data.description: Observational, statistical, computational, or radiative-transfer methods specifically useful for interstellar-medium and star-formation research, such as spectral decomposition, gas tomography, map reconstruction, molecular or atomic line analysis, and dedicated ISM surveys.

solar_physics.description: Solar physics focused on the Sun, solar flares, coronal heating, solar wind, sunspots, helioseismology, or Solar Orbiter instrumentation, without a direct interstellar-medium or star-formation objective.

stellar_atmospheres_evolution.description: Individual-star physics such as stellar atmospheres, photospheres, stellar interiors, stellar evolution, evolved stars, red giants, red supergiants, AGB stars, stellar rotation, or mass loss when the ISM is only background context.

planetary_disks_exoplanets.description: Planet formation, protoplanetary or debris disks, exoplanets, planetesimals, planetary atmospheres, orbital dynamics, and planetary systems when the molecular cloud or star-forming environment is not the scientific focus.

compact_objects_transients.description: Compact-object and transient astrophysics focused on black holes, neutron stars, pulsars, X-ray binaries, gamma-ray bursts, accretion disks, relativistic jets, gravitational waves, or neutrino transients rather than the ISM.

galaxy_evolution_agn.description: Extragalactic galaxy evolution, AGN, galaxy populations, galaxy-scale metallicity calibration, cosmological simulations, or high-redshift galaxy spectroscopy where the main goal is galaxy evolution rather than the physics of the interstellar medium itself.

cosmology_large_scale_structure.description: Cosmology and large-scale structure including dark matter, dark energy, cosmological parameters, CMB, gravitational lensing, galaxy clustering, and early-universe physics unrelated to the Galactic or local ISM.

generic_instrumentation.description: General telescope, detector, calibration, pipeline, spectroscopy, or instrumentation development whose scientific application is broad and not specifically motivated by interstellar-medium or star-formation measurements.
